For the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{5}=1\), \(a=3,\;b=\sqrt5,\;c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}=2\).  
The foci are \(F(2,0)\) and \(F'(-2,0)\). The perimeter of \(\triangle APF\) is
\[
\mathcal P=AP+PF+FA,
\]
and \(FA\) is constant, so maximizing \(\mathcal P\) is equivalent to maximizing \(AP+PF\).

By the ellipse definition, \(PF+PF'=2a=6\), hence
\[
AP+PF=6+(AP-PF').
\]
For any point \(P\), the triangle inequality gives \(AP-PF'\le AF'\), with equality iff \(A,F',P\) are collinear and \(F'\) lies between \(A\) and \(P\). Since \(AF'=\sqrt{(0+2)^2+(2\sqrt3)^2}=4\), the maximum of \(AP+PF\) is \(6+4=10\).

The line \(AF'\) has equation \(y=\sqrt3\,x+2\sqrt3\). Substituting into the ellipse yields
\[
\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{3(x+2)^2}{5}=1\;\Longrightarrow\;x=-\frac34\ \text{or}\ x=-\frac{21}{8}.
\]
The point beyond \(F'\) (so that \(F'\) is between \(A\) and \(P\)) is \(P\!\left(-\frac{21}{8},-\frac{5\sqrt3}{8}\right)\).

The area of \(\triangle APF\) is
\[
\frac12\Bigl|\det\bigl(\overrightarrow{FA},\overrightarrow{FP}\bigr)\Bigr|
=\frac12\left|
\begin{vmatrix}
-2 & 2\sqrt3\\[2pt]
-\frac{37}{8} & -\frac{5\sqrt3}{8}
\end{vmatrix}
\right|
=\frac{21\sqrt3}{4}.
\]

=\frac{21\sqrt3}{4}.$$
